results.title: From Nov 18, China wants a licence before tunnel-boring machines go to "sensitive countries and regions that have disputes with China".
results.description:
From Nov 18, China wants a licence before tunnel-boring machines go to "sensitive countries and regions that have disputes with China".

@MOFCOM_China didn't name India. It didn't need to.

Look at the list. Tunnel-boring machines and key parts like cutterheads. Walking excavators for rough ground. And wet shotcrete machines made for work above 3,000 metres. Those spray concrete inside tunnels at high altitude. Think Himalayan roads and border tunnels.

Beijing says it's about national security.

Why it matters for us.

India depends on imports for these machines. Metro lines, rail corridors and border tunnels all need them. Orders for India have been stuck at Chinese customs since 2024. @PiyushGoyalOffc raised it with Germany that year, as a German firm's China-made machines were held up.

Now that delay has a legal process behind it.

Delhi is calm so far. Officials told ET they don't expect a big slowdown in highway building. One flagged risk to some critical projects, including the bullet train. A scheme to boost local making of this equipment is close to final approval. @hd_kumaraswamy said last month that about ₹45,000 crore of equipment and parts depend heavily on imports.

My bet: no outright ban. China grants licences slowly, case by case, and keeps the tap as a lever on Delhi. At least one Indian metro or rail project reports a machine delay by March 2027. The local scheme gets cleared before the Feb 2027 Budget.

Watch the first licence call on a pending Indian order after Nov 18.

results.title: Expected after India’s Ladakh naming, the FM’s trade-barrier callouts & tighter FDI PN3 scrutiny for China.
results.description:
Expected after India’s Ladakh naming, the FM’s trade-barrier callouts & tighter FDI PN3 scrutiny for China.

Chinese are posturing. Beijing rarely imposes permanent bans; expect waivers. Licensing bottlenecks create uncertain lead times for Indian EPC contractors pricing Chinese equip—next 'case-by-case' waivers may force contractors to disclose precise project locations & site data to MOFCOM to prove "non-military" use.

Bottomline: suit up & invest—or suck up and stop the border posturing without sufficient leverage.

Would you supply equipment to someone who might use it against you?

results.title: 🇨🇳🇮🇳 China has announced export controls on tunnel-boring machines, with restrictions taking effect November 18.
results.description:
🇨🇳🇮🇳 China has announced export controls on tunnel-boring machines, with restrictions taking effect November 18.

The move could complicate India’s procurement of tunnelling equipment for metro, railway, and strategic border projects, risking supply delays.

The development underscores India’s need to boost domestic manufacturing and reduce dependence on China for critical infrastructure technology.
